root_cause.text: Missing bounds check on the address parameter length before reading the address in __sctp_rcv_asconf_lookup(), allowing an unauthenticated peer to trigger reading uninitialized memory beyond a truncated ASCONF chunk.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explains that the function "only checks that the ASCONF chunk can hold the ADDIP header and a parameter header, then calls af->from_addr_param(), which reads the full address ... trusting the parameter's declared length." It adds that a peer can send a truncated trailing ASCONF chunk declaring an IPv6 address parameter but stopping after the parameter header, causing from_addr_param() to read uninitialized bytes. The patch adds the check `if (sizeof(*asconf) + ntohs(param->p.length) > ntohs(ch->length)) return NULL;` to verify the address parameter lies within the chunk.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential out-of-bounds read in __sctp_rcv_asconf_lookup by validating the address parameter's length against the chunk boundary.
intent_record.what: Added a boundary check before accessing the address parameter in an ASCONF chunk to ensure the parameter's declared length does not exceed the chunk length.
intent_record.how: The new if-statement compares the offset total (sizeof(*asconf) + ntohs(param->p.length)) against the chunk's total length (ntohs(ch->length)). If it exceeds, the function returns NULL early, preventing any subsequent reads of out-of-bounds data.
